title: ReleaseGraph plan v1 (graph view)
description: What `releasegraph plan --graph <file> --state <file>|--live --output json` writes to stdout, as consumed by .github/workflows/reusable-readonly-plan.yml. Scope is deliberately narrow. `releasegraph plan --path <policy>` is a different command with a different shape: its `blocked` is an array of ids and it also emits `nodes`. That shape is NOT described here, because one schema cannot honestly cover two incompatible payloads that share a property name. `blocked` here always means the graph view's map of project id to unsatisfied dependency ids.

error.description: Declared by the CLI envelope and currently NEVER emitted: no command sets it, and a failing plan writes human-readable text to stderr with a non-zero exit code and no JSON at all. It stays in this schema because the type declares it; see docs/plan.md.

graphView.description: A plan is computed from fresh state, never stored. Ready means every dependency condition holds; blocked names the ones that do not; noop means there is nothing to do.

ready.description: Project ids whose dependencies are satisfied and which are not HEALTHY.

blocked.description: Project id -> the dependency ids whose condition is unsatisfied.

noop.description: Project ids already HEALTHY: a released version is never re-released for its own sake.

stateInput.description: The `--state <file>` input: project id -> node state. Any string decodes (the loader does not validate), but only these values are meaningful; an unrecognised value is treated as not-HEALTHY, so it plans work rather than skipping it. Repo-health values (schemas/health-v1.json) are a subset.

healthValue.description: Node state vocabulary: every internal/domain.Health value, because the state file describes a node's current state, not a repository report. Only HEALTHY means there is nothing to do; any other value makes the project a planning candidate. This is deliberately WIDER than schemas/health-v1.json, whose values are the narrower repository-health subset: the fixture in testdata/graph/diamond-health.json uses READY, which is transaction state and would be rejected as repository health.
